# Premenstrual pattern detection: synthetic evaluation

**Generated by:** `node tools/premenstrual-eval.mjs 1500 20261127` on 2026-11-27.

**Synthetic people only.** Every generator setting is an ASSUMPTION (below), not a measured population value. This shows how the two rules behave on the same people, not how accurate either is for real people.

## Assumptions (uniform draws per person)
| Setting | Range |
|---|---|
| Complete cycles per person | 6 |
| Her mean cycle length (days) | 25–33 |
| Her cycle-to-cycle SD (days) | 1–6 |
| Chance of strong cravings on any day (background) | 0.03–0.25 |
| Chance on each of the 5 days before a period (pattern group only) | 0.5–0.9 |
| Chance she logs on a given day | 0.4–0.95 |

## People with NO premenstrual pattern: told they have a cravings pattern (false patterns; lower is better)
| Method | Result |
|---|---|
| Older forward finder (patterns.js, counts from day 1) | 484 of 1500 (**32.3%**, 95% CI 29.9%–34.7%) |
| Strict ACOG rule (5 days before; nothing notable on days 5–12) | 10 of 1500 (**0.7%**, 95% CI 0.4%–1.2%) |
| C-PASS rule, the app's rule (days −7..−1 vs days 4..10; rise ≥ 30% of the scale) | 7 of 1500 (**0.5%**, 95% CI 0.2%–1.0%) |

## People WITH a premenstrual pattern: pattern found (higher is better)
| Method | Result |
|---|---|
| Older forward finder | 1349 of 1500 (**89.9%**, 95% CI 88.3%–91.4%) |
| Strict ACOG rule | 213 of 1500 (**14.2%**, 95% CI 12.5%–16.1%) |
| C-PASS rule (the app's rule) | 504 of 1500 (**33.6%**, 95% CI 31.3%–36.0%) |

**Subgroup: a clear pattern (chance on the days before a period ≥ 0.7) and logging most days (≥ 0.7):** C-PASS found 176 of 342 (**51.5%**); the older finder 338 of 342.

## Reading this
- **False patterns are what matter most:** telling someone "this is your pattern" when it isn't is the failure that makes an app sound clever while being wrong. Both new rules keep it below 1%; the older finder told about 1 in 3 people with no pattern that they had one.
- The older finder reports a pattern at ANY cycle day, so it is not specific to the days before a period. The new rules look only at the days before a period, compared with the week after.
- The strict rule misses most patterns: one occasional symptom in the week after cancels a cycle. C-PASS compares averages, so it tolerates that.
- Both new rules need the symptom in each of her last 3 cycles with logs on both sides. People who log rarely, or whose pattern is weak, are told "still learning" or nothing, rather than something wrong.
- The detection rates depend entirely on the assumed pattern strengths above. They are not estimates of real-world detection.
- Not tested: real people. mcPHASES (PhysioNet access pending) may include daily symptom data to check this on; to be confirmed.
